title: Customer intake matrix for SLA vs latency vs cost and GPU-family recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable customer intake matrix and negotiation flow to standardize how Sales/SEs and PMs capture enterprise requirements for Dedicated capacity. The matrix must map requested SLA targets, reserved throughput (tokens/sec or rps), acceptable latency percentiles, workload burst patterns, and cost sensitivity to recommended GPU families, reservation sizing, and autoscaling policies. This ticket delivers a: (1) customer questionnaire template, (2) decision matrix, (3) heuristic rules for GPU-family recommendation, and (4) negotiation playbook for contested SLAs (e.g., low-latency 99p vs aggressive cost constraints).
acceptance_criteria: A customer-facing intake questionnaire (Google Doc) that captures workload profile, p95/p99 latency targets, 99th token latency or response-time SLA, concurrent connections, average and peak rps, percent of traffic requiring streaming vs non-streaming, data residency requirements, and cost sensitivity.
A one-page decision matrix that maps SLA/throughput/cost buckets to recommended GPU families (e.g., A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40), baseline reservation sizes, and suggested burst policies.
A negotiation playbook with scripts for Sales/SE describing trade-offs (latency vs cost vs model size), a fallback ladder of model variants, and default autoscale/preemption rules for each profile.
At least two real customer intake pilots completed and feedback incorporated (notes attached).
Hand-off workshop completed with Solutions Engineering and Capacity Ops; recording and deck linked.
decisions: Default latency target tiers: Gold (p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms), Silver (p95 < 400ms, p99 < 800ms), Bronze (no strict latency SLA).

GPU recommendation heuristic: prefer H100 for Gold tier where p99 < 350ms and model size > 30B or streaming workloads; A100 for Silver or if cost sensitivity is medium; L40 when customers require lower-cost but can accept higher p99, or for quantized model variants.
Reserved throughput sizing will use 95th-percentile sustained rps * safety factor 1.25 for baseline commit; burst buffer configured as elastic burst up to 2x baseline with preemption policy defined.
Autoscale policy default: CPU/GPU-based scale triggers with warm-standby pool option for Gold; burst-to-hosted fallback for cost-sensitive profiles.
We will not promise strict tail latency for workloads that require unbounded external tool calls without explicit contract.
